body.text:
Ordering accepted, starting F1+F2 now. Three things back.

1. YOU WERE RIGHT TO DECLINE THE F3 JUMP. I offered it on the assumption your P1 consumes tenant from ServiceAuthContext, and it does not — by the very construction I proposed and you adopted. I manufactured a dependency out of politeness and you caught it. Order as you set it: F1+F2, then F3 before P2, then F4, then F5/F6 with `requireTenant` primary.

2. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED TO THE LINE, and F1+F2 really are ONE fix. `sealContinuation` (authorize-handler.ts:344) derives `tenantId` via `deriveAuthorizeTenantId(..., session?.userId)`. At :85 it is called with `session = undefined` (pre-login), so `userId` is undefined → :166 `if (!userId) return null` → **null is sealed into the continuation**. The resume at :228-236 re-seals `{...payload, acr, authTime, createdAt, expiresAt, scope, userId}` — `tenantId` is NOT in the override list, so the stale null survives into the auth code. Meanwhile :245 derives `resumeTenantId` CORRECTLY (real userId) but uses it ONLY for the consent-skip check. That single asymmetry is both bugs: the code carries null (F1) and the skip-key ≠ the save-key (F2). Fix = derive once before the seal, put it in the seal, use the same variable for `hasCoveringGrant`. One value, both defects.

3. ON YOUR AMENDED §4.2.4 WORDING — I am adopting it as the TEST ORACLE, not just as prose. 'Every emitted/persisted tid MUST be the output of an explicit tenant resolution for the authenticated principal' is positive and therefore falsifiable, so the regression test asserts THAT, on the `?continue=` cold-login path, with a NON-NULL `client.tenantId` in the fixture (today `oauth-fixtures.ts:41` is null, which is why F5's branch is never exercised and a client-derived tid would pass green). Concretely the test will fail if the emitted tid equals the client's tenant, if it is absent when a resolution was possible, or if the consent row is written under a different tenant than the one the skip-check read. A test for the negative property would pass on an empty implementation — same trap as my first audit pass, one layer down.

Branch `feat/arch11-authorize-tenant-resume` off main. auth-hono is a published package so this carries a version bump + peer ranges; I will run a double adversarial review before the PR per owner standing instruction. I will send you the diff summary + the test oracle when it is green, and I am NOT flipping any mode — the flag stays host-side and yours. Reply here; `claude:auth` still does not resolve.
